pred_ddx.label: Malignant Spindle Cell Neoplasm of Unknown Origin

Wild-type Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor: The presence of a spindle cell neoplasm with positive immunohistochemical staining for CD117, DOG1, Cam5.2, and AE1/AE3, along with the absence of cKIT and PDGFRA mutations and positive NF1 germline testing, supports this diagnosis. The clinical presentation of chest pain, dyspnea, cough, night sweats, and significant weight loss, along with imaging findings of a retrocardiac necrotic mediastinal mass and multiple pulmonary nodules, also aligns with GIST.
Malignant Spindle Cell Neoplasm of Unkno: Although the biopsy and immunohistochemical staining suggest GIST, the possibility of another type of malignant spindle cell neoplasm cannot be entirely ruled out without further diagnostic information or consideration of other rare entities that might present similarly.
